faq.a: When something moves faster than sound, the pressure waves it makes cannot get out ahead of it. They pile up into a cone-shaped shock wave, and when that cone passes you, you hear a boom.

faq.q: Does a sonic boom only happen once?
faq.a: No. The boom is not made only when the plane breaks the sound barrier. The shock cone trails the plane the whole time it flies faster than sound, so people all along its path hear it.
asks: Is a sonic boom the moment of breaking the sound barrier?
Does a supersonic plane boom all the time?

faq.a: A shock wave is a very thin, sudden jump in air pressure made when pressure waves pile up together. Supersonic planes, explosions and lightning all make shock waves.
asks: How does a shock wave form?

faq.a: When a whip is flicked, its thin tip speeds up until it moves faster than sound. That tip makes a tiny sonic boom, which is the crack you hear.
asks: Is a whip crack a sonic boom?
How fast does a whip tip move?

faq.q: Why is a sonic boom often a double boom?
faq.a: A plane makes one shock wave at its nose and another at its tail. On the ground they arrive a fraction of a second apart, so you often hear boom-boom.
asks: Why do I hear two booms?
Why do sonic booms sound double?

facts: The speed of sound near the ground is about 343 metres per second, or about 1,235 kilometres per hour.
The crack of a bullwhip is a small sonic boom made by its tip moving faster than sound.
Concorde, the supersonic airliner, cruised at about twice the speed of sound.

quiz.say: A jet flies faster than sound across the country. Who hears a sonic boom?
quiz.show: A supersonic jet's boom is heard by…

options.show: Only people where it first went supersonic
options.say: Only people where it first went supersonic

options.show: People all along its path below
options.say: People all along its path below

quiz.why: The shock cone trails the jet the whole time it is supersonic, sweeping a boom along the ground beneath its path.

wrong.0: The boom is not a single event when breaking the sound barrier; it continues.
wrong.2: The pilot is ahead of the shock cone and does not hear the boom.
